body.p: Badly lived one human, an orphan. He had neither clothing nor footwear. He lived nude. He thought: "How will I live alone?" If I go away, I will find, meet people". He went outside and went wherever his eyes led him. Once he saw a river appeared, a big river is seen. He comes down there, comes down, a big river is there. He looks down, a long reach and a fish weir are visible. "I came there, I cut tree pole bunches. The poles are too big to catch. I see a trace, apparently, two-feet big. There is a trace of a a bailer, of its bolt. He looks down, it is a big bailer, a big bailer. "Down the river I see a devil coming". He got frightened. "I came earlier, I will stay here. [Even] if he eats me, I will still be here. Here he comes. He sees me. "A dolly! My daughter will play [with you]. I will probably take you with me". He put him into his mitten. He went home with him. The human is sitting in the mitten. He looks upwards, a big tent is standing there. He came. He carries [dolly] into the tent. "Daughter, I found a dolly, play." They live. His old woman says to him: "Old man, make a bow, for a human, who used to live by himself, [could] eat meat of a wild animal". The old man makes a bow. "Let them [both] go". He makes ski. That human [dolly] skis. He takes his bow. The old man himself goes just like that, without ski. Once he sees a reindeer trace. He catches up [= follows the trail]. Dolly is skiing forward, telling him, that he sees a reindeer with his own eyes. He shoots one buck. He [the old man?] sits down. Then the old man comes back. He sees a buck lying, the dolly is sitting tired. The old man says: "I see Opsja, I will bring [it] home". He goes away.[OSV:] not sure in the correct interpretation of the word "opsÃ¤", but according to IES it can be the name of the doll. He breakes one larch with his hands. He stuck the buck with its fur of legs into the middle [of the larch] (?). "Let's go home". He came home. [When] the old man brought Opsja, the old woman said so: "Good dolly". They live, their [OSV:] not sure in the correct interpretation of the word "opsÃ¤", but according to IES it can be the name of the doll.daughter and the dolly play together. She gave birth to a child, her son grows. Once the old man [says]: "Let's let our daughter and her partner go.[OSV:] Here the verb "qoqo" has the meaning "to give birth". The dolly's people are waiting at home." The old man and the old woman gave their daughter away. Their daughter's [partner?] went away. It is bad to live here at home. The giant old man, having given away his daughter's husband, sent [his] son to the Selkup land, to the river Taz. The giant's daughter came to the old man's land.
